title: PHOTO GALLERY: Lady Patriots end Lady Chiefs' season - NewsBreak
text:
By STAFF REPORT ,
9 hours ago
RUTLEDGE — The Cherokee Lady Chiefs saw their historic season come to an end on Tuesday, Oct. 13 in the semifinal round of the Region 1-AA volleyball tournament at Grainger High School.
The Lady Chiefs fell to a very good Sullivan East Lady Patriots team in straight sets 25-7, 25-14 and 25-18.
“I’m really proud of the girls. It wasn’t the outcome that we expected, but it was a big court to play on and a big word to hear when we talked about region,” said Cherokee head coach McKenzie Brewer.
“We had never been put on that court before past third place in districts, so to be able to walk away from this season and know we’ve changed school history and changed the volleyball program for Cherokee High School means a lot to me and I know it means a lot to these girls, especially the seniors,” Brewer said.
Cherokee says goodbye to six seniors, who Brewer said have poured their hearts and souls into the program. They are Kenzie Collins, Shelby Helton, Kelsie Henley, Maggie Jones, Abby Shanks and Trinity Williams.
Sullivan East, the District 1-AA champion, didn’t waste any time taking charge.
The Lady Patriots came out strong, leading 13-0 in the first set before the Lady Chiefs scored and won 25-7. The Lady Chiefs faired better in the second set, tying the score 7-7 before the Lady Patriots pulled away for the 25-14 win. The third set was tied 9-9 before the Lady Patriots put it away for the 25-18 win.
“I feel like the girls played their hearts out all season for us and we learned a lot. That’s all I could ask for, and I’m extremely proud of them,” Brewer said.
Elizabethton bounced back from a tough first-set loss to defeat Grainger 3-1 (23-25, 25-21, 25-17, 25-21) in the other semifinal to make it an all District 1 championship match.
In the title bout, also held Tuesday at Grainger, Sullivan East defeated Elizabethton 3-1 (23-25, 25-17, 25-22, 25-22) to capture their second straight Region 1-AA volleyball championship. Makayla Moore posted 24 kills and eight digs for the Lady Patriots in the title match and was named the region tournament MVP.
Cherokee junior Chloe Pearson was named to the Region 1-AA all-tournament team.
Both Sullivan East and Elizabethton advanced to the TSSAA sectional round on Thursday, Oct. 15 to play for a berth in the state tournament. East hosts Alcoa, while Elizabethton travels to Seymour (22-6). The sectional winners move on to the Class AA state quarterfinals on Oct. 20 in Murfreesboro. Results of Thursday’s sectional contests were not available at deadline for the Weekend e-edition.
